title: CAVC Demonstrates 1.10-1.35x Inference Acceleration in Audio-Visual Generation
summary: Benchmarking in preprint 2610.30854 reports 1.10x to 1.35x wall-clock acceleration across public benchmarks using modality-asymmetric caching while maintaining audio fidelity and cross-modal synchronization.
research_notes:
Identify the cache-tolerant regime in the sampling trajectory of the joint audio-visual diffusion model, typically corresponding to intermediate diffusion timesteps.

Configure the sampling loop to cache and reuse audio denoiser outputs and bypass cross-modal attention during the intermediate phase while maintaining full un-cached video denoiser execution.

Restore full joint audio-visual denoising across both modalities for the final terminal steps to eliminate cross-modal drift and lock audio-visual synchronization.

Avoid caching video denoiser outputs across intermediate sampling steps, as video representations lack the asymmetric recoverability of audio and suffer irrecoverable temporal blur and motion degradation.

Ensure a sufficient window of terminal joint denoising steps is preserved at the end of the sampling trajectory to guarantee audio fidelity and precise temporal alignment with video dynamics.
